medfit Cookbook

Source: vignettes/articles/cookbook.qmd

Twenty-one task-sized recipes. Each says when to use it, runs on mediation_demo (except the cluster and latent-mediator recipes, which simulate their data), and links to the article that explains it. For a one-page lookup see the Reference Card.

These recipes need medfit 0.8.0 or later (recipes 18 and 19 need 0.9.0, recipe 20 and the native route in recipe 7 need 0.10.0, and recipe 21 needs 0.11.0). CRAN has 0.3.2, which lacks mediation_demo and the native, joint and cluster functions; install from GitHub or r-universe (see the home page).

library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
covs <- c("covariate1", "covariate2")

1. One-line mediation

When: one mediator, one outcome, a data frame, and you want an answer now.

res <- med(mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
           outcome = "outcome", covariates = covs)
quick(res)
NIE = 0.333  | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 %

More: Getting Started.

2. I already have lm fits

When: you fitted the mediator and outcome models yourself.

fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
            mediation_demo)
x <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y,
                       treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
tidy(x, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 3 × 5
  term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.333    0.0645  0.206       0.459
2 nde      0.206    0.110  -0.00936     0.421
3 te       0.539    0.119   0.304       0.773

More: Model Extraction.

3. Binary outcome

When: the outcome is 0/1. Fit the outcome with glm(); the b path and c' are on the logit scale.

fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
d <- mediation_demo
d$outcome_bin <- as.integer(d$outcome > median(d$outcome))
fit_yb <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
              data = d, family = binomial())
xb <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_yb,
                        treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")
paths(xb)
        a         b   c_prime
0.5826425 0.8632919 0.1271924

More: Model Extraction.

4. Weights and robust standard errors

When: inverse-probability weights, or case weights for independent observations. Pair them with se_type = "sandwich"; model-based standard errors are not valid under inverse-probability weights. The sandwich (HC3) standard errors treat the observations as independent, so they do not handle survey clusters, strata or replicate weights.

ps <- glm(treatment ~ covariate1 + covariate2, family = binomial(),
          data = mediation_demo)
p_t <- fitted(ps)
p_m <- mean(mediation_demo$treatment)
ipw <- ifelse(mediation_demo$treatment == 1, p_m / p_t, (1 - p_m) / (1 - p_t))
xw <- fit_mediation(
  outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  weights = ipw, se_type = "sandwich"
)
tidy(xw, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 3 × 5
  term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.335    0.0657   0.206      0.463
2 nde      0.208    0.115   -0.0180     0.433
3 te       0.542    0.119    0.308      0.776

More: Getting Started.

5. Two mediators in a chain

When: treatment, then mediator 1, then mediator 2, then outcome. Put every mediator in the outcome model.

fit_m1 <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_m2 <- lm(mediator2 ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             mediation_demo)
fit_ys <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + mediator2 + covariate1 +
               covariate2, mediation_demo)
xs <- extract_mediation(fit_m1, model_y = fit_ys, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        mediator_models = list(fit_m2))
c(chain = unname(nie(xs)), every_path = unname(nie(xs, type = "total")),
  total = unname(te(xs)))
     chain every_path      total
0.07545039 0.36740438 0.53856776

nie() is the full chain a d b; type = "total" adds the paths that skip a mediator. More: Model Extraction.

6. Two mediators side by side

When: both mediators are driven by the treatment, neither by the other.

fit_m1 <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_m3 <- lm(mediator3 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_yp <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + mediator3 + covariate1 +
               covariate2, mediation_demo)
xp <- extract_mediation(fit_m1, model_y = fit_yp, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator3"),
                        mediator_models = list(fit_m3), structure = "parallel")
paths(xp)
       a1        b1        a2        b2   c_prime
0.5826425 0.5685676 0.4760604 0.2124038 0.1061791 
nie(xp)
Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.4324

The effect is the sum of the per-mediator products. More: Model Extraction.

7. Treatment-by-mediator interaction

When: the outcome model has treatment * mediator. You get the four-way decomposition (CDE, INTref, INTmed, PIE) at a reference mediator level m_star.

fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_yi <- lm(outcome_int ~ treatment * mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             mediation_demo)
xi <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_yi, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = "mediator1", m_star = 0)
decompose(xi)
       cde    int_ref    int_med        pie        nde        nie      total
0.21521278 0.04353909 0.27709549 0.34001758 0.25875187 0.61711307 0.87586495

The native engine gives the same parts from model syntax (0.10.0 or later): write the product as treatment:mediator1. The fit warns once that the global model test is not available for a product of a regression target.

sem_i <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
   outcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2",
  mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich"
))
decompose(extract_mediation(sem_i, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                            outcome = "outcome_int"))
       cde    int_ref    int_med        pie        nde        nie      total
0.21521278 0.04353909 0.27709549 0.34001758 0.25875187 0.61711307 0.87586495

More: Model Extraction, the native product term.

8. Many mediators with products

When: several mediators and a treatment-by-mediator term. The result is the joint effect over the mediator block; bootstrap it with joint_effects().

fit_m1 <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, mediation_demo)
fit_m2 <- lm(mediator2 ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             mediation_demo)
fit_yj <- lm(outcome_int ~ treatment * mediator1 + mediator2 + covariate1 +
               covariate2, mediation_demo)
xj <- extract_mediation(fit_m1, model_y = fit_yj, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        mediator_models = list(fit_m2))
boot_j <- bootstrap_mediation(
  function(theta) joint_effects(xj, theta)[["nie"]],
  method = "parametric", mediation_data = xj, n_boot = 1000, seed = 1
)
c(estimate = unname(nie(xj)), lower = boot_j@ci_lower, upper = boot_j@ci_upper)
 estimate     lower     upper
0.6560315 0.4397306 0.8950371

More: Methods and Formulas.

9. Cluster-randomized trial

When: the treatment is assigned to whole clusters (schools) and the mediator and outcome are measured on individuals. Formulas hold fixed effects only; the engine adds the random cluster intercept.

set.seed(2026)
J <- 40
n <- 10
cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n)
x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J))
v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)
u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)
cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl])
cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n)
mbar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school)
cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * (cdat$M - mbar) + 0.6 * mbar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n)
xc <- fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat, treatment = "X",
                    mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school")
tidy(xc, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 5 × 5
  term      estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie         0.209     0.127  -0.0397      0.458
2 nde         0.0772    0.227  -0.368       0.522
3 te          0.287     0.241  -0.186       0.760
4 own         0.103     0.0543 -0.00323     0.210
5 spillover   0.106     0.0886 -0.0675      0.280
decompose(xc)
      own spillover       nie
0.1032345 0.1061099 0.2093444
attr(,"label")
[1] "cluster-average, large-cluster approximation"

With few clusters add se_type = "kr" (needs pbkrtest), and bootstrap whole clusters for the product effects:

nie_of <- function(dd) {
  unname(nie(fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = dd, treatment = "X",
                           mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school")))
}
boot_c <- bootstrap_mediation(
  nie_of, method = "nonparametric", data = cdat, cluster = "school",
  n_boot = 200, seed = 123
)
Warning in .bootstrap_nonparametric_cluster(data, statistic_fn, n_boot, : 3
bootstrap samples failed and were excluded (3 of them singular or
non-convergent refits)
boot_c
BootstrapResult object
======================

Method:   nonparametric
Estimate:   0.2093
N bootstrap samples: 197

95% Confidence Interval:
  Lower:  -0.0038
  Upper:   0.5241

The warning, when it appears, counts the draws dropped as singular or non-convergent refits; the interval uses the rest. The own and spillover split is a large-cluster approximation, and the interval evidence for the cluster bootstrap is for other designs; see Methods and Formulas and Bootstrap Inference.

10. I use lavaan

When: you fitted the model as a structural equation model. The same accessors apply.

syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + c_prime * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
"
sem_fit <- lavaan::sem(syntax, data = mediation_demo)
xl <- extract_mediation(sem_fit, treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = "mediator1", outcome = "outcome")
tidy(xl, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 3 × 5
  term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.333    0.0642  0.207       0.459
2 nde      0.206    0.109  -0.00801     0.420
3 te       0.539    0.119   0.306       0.771

More: Model Extraction.

11. A latent mediator, native engine

When: the mediator is a construct measured by several indicators, and you want its indirect effect without first averaging the indicators into a score. The mediator eta is not a column of the data; the model syntax defines it.

set.seed(11)
n <- 400
X <- rnorm(n)
eta <- 0.5 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.9)
ldat <- data.frame(
  X = X,
  m1 = eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),
  m2 = 0.8 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),
  m3 = 0.7 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8)
)
ldat$Y <- 0.4 * eta + 0.2 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8)
syntax <- "
  eta =~ m1 + m2 + m3
  eta ~ a * X
  Y ~ b * eta + cp * X
"
xs <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = ldat, treatment = "X",
                    mediator = "eta", engine = "native")
tidy(xs, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 3 × 5
  term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 nie      0.169    0.0310    0.108     0.229
2 nde      0.255    0.0487    0.159     0.350
3 te       0.423    0.0445    0.336     0.510

fit_sem() fits the same syntax and returns the SEMFit. mbco_sem() tests the indirect effect as the minimum of two likelihood-ratio tests, refitting with a == 0 and with b == 0:

mbco_sem(fit_sem(syntax, ldat), "a", "b")

    Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect

data:  a * b = 0
MBCO = 46.753, df = 1, p-value = 8.054e-12

12. A nonlinear constraint or a longer chain, native engine

When: you want to fix the direct effect at the indirect effect (cp == a*b), or test the indirect effect of a three-mediator-step chain, which is a product of three paths. Constraints may be nonlinear in the labels.

base <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment
"
free <- fit_sem(base, mediation_demo)
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "cp == a * b"), mediation_demo)
rbind(free = coef(free)[c("a", "b", "cp")], tied = coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")])
             a         b         cp
free 0.4559961 0.7134287 0.04057665
tied 0.3381172 0.6831633 0.23098930

The tied fit has one more degree of freedom and its standard errors respect the constraint. anova(tied, free) is the likelihood-ratio test of it. For a chain a, d, b, mbco_sem() takes the paths and returns the minimum of the single-path tests, referred to a chi-square with one degree of freedom (conservative when several paths are zero):

chain <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  mediator2 ~ d * mediator1 + treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator2 + mediator1 + treatment
"
mbco_sem(fit_sem(chain, mediation_demo), paths = c("a", "d", "b"))

    Minimum-of-3 likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect

data:  a * d * b = 0
MBCO = 17.557, df = 1, p-value = 2.788e-05

13. Joint significance for a binary or count outcome

When: the outcome is binary or a count and you want to know whether the mediated path exists, without an outcome-scale effect. Test a = 0 and b = 0 separately and take the larger p-value (conservative). Each test is a likelihood-ratio test for a binomial or Poisson model and an F test for a Gaussian, Gamma or quasi* model, whose dispersion is estimated.

d <- mediation_demo
d$outcome_bin <- as.integer(d$outcome > median(d$outcome))
joint_test <- function(fit_a, term_a, fit_b, term_b) {
  one <- function(fit, term) {
    known <- fit$family$family %in% c("binomial", "poisson")
    col <- if (known) "Pr(>Chi)" else "Pr(>F)"
    drop1(fit, scope = term, test = if (known) "LRT" else "F")[term, col]
  }
  p <- c(a = one(fit_a, term_a), b = one(fit_b, term_b))
  c(p, joint = max(p))
}
fit_a <- glm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d)
fit_b <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             data = d, family = binomial())
joint_test(fit_a, "treatment", fit_b, "mediator1")
           a            b        joint
8.096703e-09 2.024938e-12 8.096703e-09

More: GLM families.

14. Compare two native models

When: you want to know whether a path or a constraint is needed, on the native engine. anova() is the likelihood-ratio test for nested SEMFits; it refits nothing. glance() gives AIC and BIC side by side.

full <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment
", mediation_demo)
reduced <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1
", mediation_demo)
anova(reduced, full)
Likelihood-ratio (chi-square difference) test for SEMFit models

n = 400; Chisq is n times the minimized discrepancy

        Df  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
full     0 0.0000
reduced  1 0.1335    0.13346       1     0.7149
rbind(reduced = glance(reduced)[, c("npar", "chisq", "AIC", "BIC")],
      full = glance(full)[, c("npar", "chisq", "AIC", "BIC")])
# A tibble: 2 × 4
   npar    chisq   AIC   BIC
* <int>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
1     6 1.33e- 1 2408. 2432.
2     7 4.54e-30 2409. 2437.

The restricted model is the one with more degrees of freedom. A small chi-square difference says dropping cp costs little.

15. A defined parameter and its interval

When: you want the indirect effect, the total effect or the proportion mediated with a standard error and an interval, from one fit. Define each with :=; the delta method gives the standard error.

dfit <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
  ab := a * b
  total := cp + a * b
  pm := ab / total
", mediation_demo)
dfit@defined
   name       expr       est         se
1    ab      a * b 0.3331241 0.06436069
2 total cp + a * b 0.5373844 0.11890026
3    pm ab / total 0.6198991 0.13949633
confint(dfit)[c("ab", "total", "pm"), ]
          2.5 %    97.5 %
ab    0.2069795 0.4592688
total 0.3043441 0.7704246
pm    0.3464914 0.8933069

The interval for pm is wide because a ratio is unstable when the total is small; bootstrap_mediation() on the extracted object is the alternative.

16. Bound a variance or fix a path

When: a variance should not go below a floor, or a path is known. Write the bound or the value in the syntax and read the diagnostics: an active bound means the estimate sits on the edge.

bounded <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + 0 * treatment
  outcome ~~ lower(2) * outcome
", mediation_demo)
bounded@diagnostics$active_bounds
[1] "outcome~~outcome"
round(coef(bounded)[c("a", "b")], 3)
    a     b
0.456 0.717

lower(2) is above the variance the data want (about 1.2), so the bound binds and is reported. 0 * treatment fixes the direct effect at zero.

17. Check a native fit before trusting it

When: before you report a native fit. Read the diagnostics, then ask whether the model fits when it has restrictions (df > 0).

chk <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ treatment
  mediator2 ~ treatment
  outcome ~ mediator1 + mediator2
", mediation_demo)
chk@diagnostics[c("status", "active_bounds", "improper", "sign_check")]
$status
[1] 3

$active_bounds
character(0)

$improper
character(0)

$sign_check
[1] "ok"
glance(chk)[, c("df", "chisq", "p_value")]
# A tibble: 1 × 3
     df chisq  p_value
  <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>
1     2  138. 9.35e-31

No active bound, no improper solution and a passing sign check mean the optimizer is fine. The chi-square on 2 degrees of freedom is large, so the model leaves out something the data contain (here, the covariance of the two mediators’ residuals): the fit converged, and the model is still wrong.

More: Methods and Formulas.

18. Fix exogenous covariates (fixed_x)

When: a native model with many covariates needs many parameters, or you want to compare with lavaan’s default fixed.x = TRUE. Since 0.15.0 a native fit fixes the means, variances and covariances of the exogenous observed variables at their sample values by default (fixed_x left unset); fixed_x = FALSE estimates them instead. Left unset, fixed_x resolves to the explicit set of exogenous variables, so glance()$fixed_x names what was fixed.

syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2
  ab := a * b
"
fixed <- fit_sem(syntax, mediation_demo)
free <- fit_sem(syntax, mediation_demo, fixed_x = FALSE)
rbind(free = coef(free)[c("a", "b")], fixed_x = coef(fixed)[c("a", "b")])
                a         b
free    0.5826425 0.5996207
fixed_x 0.5826425 0.5996207
rbind(free = sqrt(diag(vcov(free)))[c("a", "b")], fixed_x = sqrt(diag(vcov(fixed)))[c("a", "b")])
                 a          b
free    0.09836668 0.05120516
fixed_x 0.09836668 0.05120516
rbind(free = free@defined[, c("est", "se")], fixed_x = fixed@defined[, c("est", "se")])
              est         se
free    0.3493645 0.06609875
fixed_x 0.3493645 0.06609875

The estimates, standard errors and the defined parameter ab agree to the digits shown. What changes is how many parameters the optimizer carries:

cbind(fit = c("free", "fixed_x"), rbind(glance(free), glance(fixed))[, c("npar", "df", "chisq", "fixed_x")])
      fit npar df    chisq                           fixed_x
1    free   19  1 3.543201
2 fixed_x   10  1 3.543201 treatment, covariate1, covariate2

The parameter count falls from 19 to 10 (the free fit also estimates the exogenous variances, covariances and means) while df and chisq stay put. glance()$fixed_x lists what is fixed ("" when nothing is). With fixed_x, the fixed rows stay in tidy() flagged fixed_x = TRUE, with no standard error, and the log likelihood, AIC() and BIC() become conditional on the fixed variables, so they differ from the free fit’s.

tf <- tidy(fixed)
tf[tf$fixed_x, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")]
# A tibble: 9 × 3
  term                   estimate std_error
  <chr>                     <dbl>     <dbl>
1 treatment~~treatment    0.250          NA
2 treatment~~covariate1  -0.0700         NA
3 treatment~~covariate2  -0.00246        NA
4 covariate1~~covariate1  1.04           NA
5 covariate1~~covariate2  0.00266        NA
6 covariate2~~covariate2  0.250          NA
7 treatment~1             0.502          NA
8 covariate1~1            0.0174         NA
9 covariate2~1            0.482          NA
tryCatch(anova(free, fixed), error = function(e) cat(conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
the fits have different `fixed_x` sets (free: none; fixed: covariate1, covariate2, treatment): their likelihoods condition on different variables, so they cannot be compared

Compare fits only when they fix the same variables. anova(), mbco_sem() and AIC()/BIC() across several fits stop when the fixed sets differ, as above. Pass a character vector (for example fixed_x = "treatment") to fix a subset.

Since 0.15.0 the default is to fix the exogenous observed variables; pass fixed_x = FALSE to keep the free exogenous block. See the 0.15.0 defaults.

More: Methods and Formulas, the native engine guide.

19. Observed intercepts and means

When: you want the intercepts of a native model, or a test of whether an intercept is zero. Since 0.15.0 every native fit has a mean structure by default (meanstructure left unset is TRUE): an intercept is free for every observed variable you did not mention, as lavaan does with meanstructure = TRUE. Writing an intercept (outcome ~ 1) is only needed to restrict it. The paths and their standard errors do not change.

paths <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment
"
free <- fit_sem(paths, mediation_demo)
tf <- tidy(free)
tf[tf$op == "~1", c("term", "estimate", "std_error")]
# A tibble: 3 × 3
  term        estimate std_error
  <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>
1 mediator1~1    0.155    0.0763
2 outcome~1      0.231    0.0774
3 treatment~1    0.502   NA

The outcome and mediator intercepts equal the lm() intercepts of the same equations. The mean of treatment is the sample mean, fixed with the other exogenous moments, so its row has no standard error. Writing outcome ~ 1 in the syntax returns the same fit, because the default already estimates that intercept.

A fixed intercept is a restriction. outcome ~ 0*1 costs one degree of freedom and changes the other estimates, so anova() can test it:

zero <- fit_sem(paste0(paths, "outcome ~ 0*1"), mediation_demo)
round(c(free = free@theta[["cp"]], fixed_at_zero = zero@theta[["cp"]]), 3)
         free fixed_at_zero
        0.041         0.262 
anova(free, zero)
Likelihood-ratio (chi-square difference) test for SEMFit models

n = 400; Chisq is n times the minimized discrepancy

     Df  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
free  0 0.0000
zero  1 8.8141     8.8141       1   0.002989 **
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
AIC(free, zero)
     df      AIC
free  7 2409.499
zero  6 2416.313

The test rejects zero, and the restricted model has the larger AIC. A fit with the mean structure off has no intercepts to restrict.

Pass meanstructure = NULL to fit a mean structure only when the model writes ~1 or a product (the 0.14.x rule), or meanstructure = FALSE for covariances only. See the 0.15.0 defaults.

More: Native engine, intercepts.

20. Four-way decomposition from a native fit

When: the outcome depends on the treatment, the mediator and their product, and you want the controlled direct effect, the two interaction terms and the pure indirect effect. Write the product as treatment:mediator1 in the outcome equation, fit with fit_sem(), and extract. A product needs the mean structure (on by default; meanstructure = FALSE is an error), so the covariate in the mediator equation enters the reference interaction through its sample mean. The fit warns that the global test is not valid with a product and recommends the sandwich covariance; the chunk silences the warning and asks for the sandwich. A factor covariate (for example a group column in the mediator equation) is expanded to dummies and enters the same way; a factor treatment or mediator is not supported, so recode a two-level factor as 0/1 first.

four_way <- "
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate2
  outcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1 + covariate2
"
fit20 <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(four_way, mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich"))
fw20 <- extract_mediation(fit20, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                          decomposition = "four_way")
tidy(fw20, type = "components", conf_int = TRUE)
# A tibble: 4 × 5
  term    estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
  <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 cde       0.0423    0.119  -0.191       0.275
2 int_ref   0.0769    0.0415 -0.00442     0.158
3 int_med   0.228     0.0707  0.0891      0.366
4 pie       0.326     0.0850  0.160       0.493

The components sum to the natural direct and indirect effects, and m_star moves the reference level of the mediator (default 0), which shifts weight between the controlled direct effect and the reference interaction.

The standard errors treat the covariate mean as fixed, so they are conditional on the observed covariates and slightly too small for a population average. To add the variance of the estimated covariate mean to INTref, the NDE and the TE, set the option below (the default stays conditional, as lavaan’s := is); the other components do not change:

op <- options(medfit.covariate_mean_variance = TRUE)
tidy(fw20, type = "components")[, c("term", "std_error")]
# A tibble: 4 × 2
  term    std_error
  <chr>       <dbl>
1 cde        0.119
2 int_ref    0.0415
3 int_med    0.0707
4 pie        0.0850
options(op)

On mediation_demo the added term is about 0.08% of the INTref standard error, so the table matches the one above to the digits shown; it matters when the interaction and the effect of the covariate on the mediator are both large (chapter 7 has a simulated case: 0.0995 becomes 0.1516 against a bootstrap SD of 0.1568).

The other route is the nonparametric bootstrap, which refits the model on each resample:

int_ref_stat <- function(dat) {
  f <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(four_way, dat))
  extract_mediation(f, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                    decomposition = "four_way")@int_ref
}
boot20 <- bootstrap_mediation(int_ref_stat, method = "nonparametric",
                              data = mediation_demo, n_boot = 200, seed = 1)
c(estimate = boot20@estimate, lower = boot20@ci_lower, upper = boot20@ci_upper)
    estimate        lower        upper
 0.076915831 -0.003651384  0.160267019

More: Native engine book, the four-way chapter, Native engine, product term.

21. A categorical covariate in a native fit

When: a covariate is a factor, character or logical column (a group, a site, a yes/no flag). Write the column name where a numeric covariate would go. The engine replaces it with one 0/1 dummy per non-reference level, named <column>_<level>; the reference is the first factor level (a character column sorts in the C locale). The rows of the fit are named mediator1~group_mid, so read them like any other path. The chunk cuts covariate1 into three groups to have a factor to use.

dat21 <- transform(mediation_demo,
                   group = cut(covariate1, c(-Inf, -0.5, 0.5, Inf), labels = c("low", "mid", "high")))
fit21 <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a*treatment + group
  outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment + group
  ind := a*b
", dat21)
tidy(fit21)[1:7, ]
# A tibble: 7 × 7
  term                 op    estimate std_error statistic  p_value fixed_x
  <chr>                <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> <lgl>
1 a                    ~        0.549    0.102       5.40 6.76e- 8 FALSE
2 mediator1~group_mid  ~        0.328    0.125       2.63 8.56e- 3 FALSE
3 mediator1~group_high ~        0.948    0.124       7.65 1.98e-14 FALSE
4 b                    ~        0.618    0.0524     11.8  3.37e-32 FALSE
5 cp                   ~        0.128    0.110       1.16 2.47e- 1 FALSE
6 outcome~group_mid    ~        0.463    0.132       3.52 4.38e- 4 FALSE
7 outcome~group_high   ~        0.729    0.139       5.25 1.53e- 7 FALSE

The estimates equal a fit with the dummies written by hand (group_mid, group_high), and a, b and ind keep their usual meaning. A label goes on one dummy, never on the factor: b*group stops with a message that names the dummies. To test one dummy, label it and constrain the label:

fit21b <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a*treatment + group
  outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment + group + z*group_mid
  z == 0
", dat21)
tidy(fit21b)[grepl("group", tidy(fit21b)$term, fixed = TRUE), ]
# A tibble: 10 × 7
   term                   op    estimate std_error statistic   p_value fixed_x
   <chr>                  <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <lgl>
 1 mediator1~group_mid    ~       0.328      0.125      2.63  8.56e- 3 FALSE
 2 mediator1~group_high   ~       0.948      0.124      7.65  1.98e-14 FALSE
 3 outcome~group_high     ~       0.474      0.120      3.94  8.11e- 5 FALSE
 4 treatment~~group_mid   ~~      0.0329    NA         NA    NA        TRUE
 5 treatment~~group_high  ~~     -0.0359    NA         NA    NA        TRUE
 6 group_mid~~group_mid   ~~      0.224     NA         NA    NA        TRUE
 7 group_mid~~group_high  ~~     -0.118     NA         NA    NA        TRUE
 8 group_high~~group_high ~~      0.228     NA         NA    NA        TRUE
 9 group_mid~1            ~1      0.338     NA         NA    NA        TRUE
10 group_high~1           ~1      0.35      NA         NA    NA        TRUE

fixed_x = "group" fixes every dummy of the factor at its sample moments, and a dummy name fixes one:

fit21c <- fit_sem("
  mediator1 ~ a*treatment + group
  outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment + group
", dat21, fixed_x = "group")
generics::glance(fit21c)$fixed_x
[1] "group_mid, group_high"

Limits: a factor as an outcome or a mediator, an ordered factor, and a product of two factors are refused with a message that says why; group:mediator1 expands to one product per dummy. A bootstrap that refits from raw data re-expands the factor in each resample, so a level missing from a character column’s resample changes the reference level.

More: Native engine, paths and defined parameters, ?"medfit-syntax" (section Factor covariates).
